author: ansel
text: Q: what counts as a code the tenant already references? A: a code the tenant itself fetched successfully from WCL in a signed-in turn (a raw_fetch_grants row: tenant, code, granted_at), written by the fetch writer from current_identity. Not a UNION over tracked_raids/recent_raids/messages: every path that references a code (chat, tracking, recent raids asked about) passes through a WCL fetch, the grant is WCL-verified (WCL itself checked access at that moment), and it needs no coupling to four RLS tables or free-text messages. Fetches with no identity (background, REST page loads) grant nothing: public-only, fails closed.

author: ansel
text: Q: how long do 'public' and a grant count? A: 7 days (RAW_STORE_REVERIFY_DAYS). After that the next read misses, WCL is asked again, which re-grants or finds the report gone and deletes it. Without a window a hot finished report served from the store would never meet a refresh, so the owner's delete-on-private rule could never fire. Not an age purge: rows are kept; only the right to serve them is re-checked.

author: ansel
text: Q: RLS on the grant table? A: yes, tenant_isolation like 0004 (it holds tenant ids + codes, i.e. what each tenant looked up). The writer sets the tenant scope per grant row. Grants are NOT deleted when a report is gone (RLS would need a cross-tenant delete): harmless, the rows they would unlock are deleted and rows only come back via a successful WCL fetch, i.e. when the code is reachable again (client credentials never see private reports). raw_fetches and the new raw_reports stay global (decision 6).

author: ansel
text: Q: unchanged payload (sc-177 AC1): skip entirely or refresh fetched_at? A: refresh fetched_at only (no payload sent or rewritten; one SELECT of hashes per batch first). Freshness needs it: a row first fetched while a report was live becomes final once refetched unchanged after the report finished. Hash = sha256 of the body with the injected _cost object removed (cost changes every request).

author: ansel
text: Q: overlong report_code / operation_name? A: no column widening. operation_name truncated to 120 (a label). report_code column set NULL when a code is over 32 chars; the code stays in report_codes (unbounded JSON) so gone-deletion still finds it. Grants/report status skip codes over 32, so such a row is never visible (fails closed). NUL: the JSON escape backslash-u0000 is removed (escape-aware: an escaped backslash followed by u0000 is kept).

author: ansel
text: Design 039 (plan/research/data-model/contracts in specs/039-local-first-data/ on branch 039-local-first-data, dev-a). (1) Visibility data model: raw_fetches stays global; new global raw_reports(code, visibility, end_time_ms, checked_at) filled from summary bodies (REPORT_SUMMARY_FIELDS gains 'code visibility'); new raw_fetch_grants(tenant_id, report_code, granted_at) with tenant RLS. A row is served to a tenant only if EVERY code it names is public (raw_reports) or granted to that tenant, each confirmed within 7 days (RAW_STORE_REVERIFY_DAYS). One function reads the table (repositories/raw_fetches.read_visible_fetch); a guard test fails if any other module selects RawFetch. (2) 'Already references' = the tenant fetched that code successfully from WCL itself in a signed-in turn (grant written by the writer from current_identity; WCL checked access then). No identity (background/REST) = no grant = public-only. (3) Read order: callers' Redis get_or_load -> loader -> AsyncWCLClient.query consults a backend-installed fetch source (like the sink) in the CALLER's context before single-flight (so a joined caller of another tenant can't ride the first caller's visibility) -> WCL. Store hit returns the stored body, back-fills Redis via the unchanged loaders, is never re-offered and grants nothing. 3 s timeout; any store error = miss. No source in CLI/evals. (4) Freshness: report rows = indefinite when the report was SEEN finished (is_finished at checked_at) and the row was fetched after it finished; otherwise only younger than WCL_CACHE_UNFINISHED_TTL (120 s, the Redis live-report rule). Non-report rows (rankings, characters, world) are never served from the store in this slice; Redis family TTLs keep governing them. (5) Private/deleted: a single-report query answered with reportData.report=null (or a summary showing visibility private) offers ReportGone through the sink queue (FIFO with writes); the writer deletes every raw_fetches row naming the code + its raw_reports row and evicts Redis wcl:v1:report:<code>:* (SCAN+DEL, glob-escaped). Grants stay (harmless). No age purge. Redis relation: it already serves report data by code to all tenants; the store is stricter (grant/public) so DB-first reads don't widen exposure; only change is eviction. sc-177: hash compare (sha256 sans _cost; same hash = fetched_at only), 20-item batch transactions with per-item retry, op name truncated, long codes NULL in report_code + never granted, NUL escape stripped, throttle flush on stop, logs = exception class + SQLSTATE. Kill switch WCL_STORE_READS_ENABLED. Carrying straight on to tasks + implementation.

author: ansel
text: Revised after my bypass review: RAW_STORE_REVERIFY_DAYS default 1 (was 7). Reason: a store hit back-fills the shared Redis entry (loaders are unchanged), so a granted tenant's hit re-warms an entry other tenants who know the code can read. Today a report made private leaves Redis within its 24 h TTL of the last WCL fetch; with the store, within window + TTL. 1 day bounds it at ~48 h (tunable) for one WCL call per tenant per report per day. Full closure (store hits not back-filling shared Redis, or tenant-aware Redis) goes to backlog, per the brief's no-Redis-redesign rule.

author: ansel
text: Backlog (from 039 bypass review): DB-first store hits back-fill the shared, tenant-less Redis entry, so the revocation lag for a report made private is window + Redis TTL (~48 h at defaults) instead of ~24 h. Options: let get_or_load skip the Redis write when the loader was answered by the store for a granted-only (non-public) row (needs a signal from client to loader), or make report families' Redis keys tenant-aware for non-public reports. Also: Redis char_reports lists still show a deleted report's code until their 5 min TTL (harmless metadata).

text: GitNexus 041: exact_report_codes CRITICAL (87, via AsyncWCLClient._fetch -> every WCL path) and _gone_codes CRITICAL (4); _run/_write CRITICAL are name collisions (other _run methods). UNKNOWN for _store_one/store_batch/upsert_raw_fetch/_report_statuses confirmed by text search: only the writer chain and its tests. Mitigation: the client changes only narrow WHEN a ReportGone is offered (never what a caller gets or raises) and exact_report_codes only gets stricter (more None = fewer store reads/grants, fail-closed). Writer changes keep the never-raise property; existing writer tests stay green.

author: ansel
text: 041 fix 1 rule (gone): a ReportGone is offered ONLY for our own REPORT_SUMMARY text (variable code, exactly stripped) answered with data.reportData.report == null, AND either (a) no errors, or (b) every error has path exactly [reportData, report] AND a message reading not-found/permission/private (case-insensitive 'not exist|no such|not found|permission|private'). Subfield errors, transient errors, any other query text (all run_wcl_graphql, our table/event queries, batch summaries) never delete. Why summary-only: it is the query every report flow fetches and its text is fixed, so aliasing/padding/directives can't reach it; table-only flows still meet revocation via the 1-day re-verify (grants expire, summary refetched). The 4 KB regex is replaced by a structural check of the parsed (tiny) body. Wrong-negative cost is bounded (<=1 day); wrong-positive cost was a global purge.

author: ansel
text: 041 fix 2 rule (grants come from the response): (a) our REPORT_SUMMARY / report_summaries_query texts grant exactly the codes whose report object came back non-null with code == requested (the parse _report_statuses already does); (b) any other query grants its one code only when its text is 'plain' (exactly one report token, code via variable with no padding, no '#', '@', '"', '...', 'fragment', no aliases) AND the body starts with data[._cost].reportData.report = {object} (anchored prefix check, no JSON parse of big bodies). Everything else grants nothing: directives, string literals, aliases, batch nulls, oversize nulls, hand-written multi-field queries. (b) keeps grants from our own table/event tool queries (the store's main value); without aliases the response key reportData.report can only be that one report field. Also exact_report_codes now returns None for a padded code (BUG-003), and rows whose codes the strict parser can't resolve get an over-approximated report_codes (every string literal and string variable) so delete-on-gone still finds them (BUG-007).

author: ansel
text: 041 fix 3: a batch that times out gets the same one-by-one retry as other errors (each item its own 10 s; order kept so a ReportGone still follows the writes before it); batches capped at 20 items AND 8 MB (the item that would overflow carries to the next batch; one oversize item still goes alone); store_batch returns the gone codes and the consumer evicts Redis after the timed DB part, under its own 5 s timeout.
